claim: SwiftUI View.glassEffect(_:in:) applies Liquid Glass to a view and is available on iOS 26.0 and newer; an app that supports iOS 17 must guard the enhancement and provide older-system behavior.

product_context.decision: Treat Liquid Glass as an optional iOS 26 enhancement candidate, not as the default visual direction.

official_sources.title: glassEffect(_:in:) | Apple Developer Documentation
supports: The modifier applies the Liquid Glass effect to a view.
The API is available on iOS 26.0 and newer.
The default variant is regular glass with a capsule shape.

version_scope.fallback: Use a regular-material capsule on iOS 17 through iOS 25, guarded by if #available(iOS 26.0, *).

checks.expected: Type checking fails because glassEffect(_:in:) requires iOS 26.0 or newer.
Type checking succeeds for an iOS 17 deployment target when the API is guarded and a fallback is present.

evidence_labels.official_source: Apple publishes the API purpose and iOS 26.0 availability.
evidence_labels.project_runtime: Xcode 26.6 type checking confirms the availability error without a guard and successful compilation with a guard for an iOS 17 target.
evidence_labels.design_inference: The API may be explored when it fits the product, but availability alone does not justify adopting Liquid Glass as the default direction.

remaining_unverified: Runtime behavior on iOS 17.5 and iOS 26.5 simulators
Accessibility, Reduce Transparency, contrast, and motion behavior
